item.title: Re: prix0rs the Cactus
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I am here per our IRC exchange to offer crit

Crit lives within
Yeeted and Deleeted

ConProcs

The temperature in its containment chamber is to be kept at a minimum of 28 degrees Celsius.

I would indicate which direction this errs. Is higher okay? Or is lower?

This is an otherwise very brief section so I have little to say. We just get right on into it and I'm good with that.

+++Description

Two arms extend from the central portion of its body.

Consider: "Two arms extend from center mass"

via levitation, usually at most 0.3 meters above the ground.

Language cleanup and significant digits. Consider: "levitation at an elevation of approximately 30cm"

SCP-XXXX is sentient and capable of speech via telepathy.

You might mean sapient. You might also want to say "communication via telepathy" rather than speech.

recording a corrupted version of its speech.

"corrupted version" is highly dubious.

It is capable of firing regular revolver ammunition

Since we just switched to the -1 I think it's probably fine, but, you could maybe stand to clarify the noun here a bit better in this passage.

bullets with a trajectory unaffected by wind,

Wind is only a factor at distances which are pretty well in excess of the range of a revolver.

It then traveled 6 kilometers across the city of Hollister,

I want to bring this up because the entire rest of this article is just one massive masquerade breach and you never cover or refer to that explicitly. There are "sightings" and nobody seems to call out the fact a levitating cactus is talking to them as it fights crime. If you want people to be nonplussed that is certainly an approach you can take, but we, as the Foundation, categorically should not be abiding this as "business as usual".

Video Logs

SCP-XXXX 'kicks' open the front door to a Starbucks.

This factually can't happen so I don't get why we're being coy. The door explodes inward, or, the door opens unassisted. This isn't very clinical even though I know exactly what you mean.

evaded capture for approximately 8 hours

This kind of begs the question of escalation. Why are we letting some random embedded agents chase this guy for a full day without sending help? Reduce the number, or send help.

technicians who smelled gunpowder in the water supply

I don't follow what this is implying and it never seems to come up again. You also probably wouldn't "smell" gunpowder; it only has a distinct smell when it's been fired/spent and that's not going to happen in water.

I liked the characterization of the video logs overall but I do have to warn you about your dialogue; you use a truly stupendous amount of exclamation points, and when they are so common they lose their meaning. Please strongly reconsider how you are applying this punctuation with an aim toward toning it down.

The best place to use an exclamation is after an interjection or command word. This is a way to suddenly or notably raise the level of emotion so you want to apply it rarely so people notice the departure from baseline. If every other line has an exclamation then that is a very excited and exhausting new baseline. I can clarify further if you want.

I would like to read this again to offer more thoughts as you explore the issues with the town, or alternatively, tighten up the timeline so those issues can be brushed away. As it stands, I am having trouble getting into what you're presenting because of the issues with the framework. I will say, in general, the central character does convey a good sense of identity but I think that their perseverance in the face of a less accommodating world might make them come through even more.

item.title: Re: prix0rs the Cactus
item.content:encoded:
[Placeholder]

Just a short foreword: I'm super bad at line-by-line because living with non-native speakers have allowed me to basically ignore most SPaG errors, so I will only point them out if they are quite jarring. Phrasing-wise too, I'll be unable to help extensively due to the same reason mentioned above.

+ show block
– hide block

The temperature to its containment chamber

'To' change to 'in'.

SCP-XXXX's other anomalous properties include mild telekinesis that mimics the usage, length and approximate strength of two human arms,

Hmm, I might just be nitpicking here, but psychokinesis would be much more suited here. Also, remove the mild, I don't think it adds much.

It is capable of firing ammunition customary of non-anomalous revolvers,

Customary just sounds plain weird. Maybe 'It is capable of firing regular revolver ammunition' would work better?

SCP-XXXX was initially seen in the neighborhood of Sprucelude Acres in Hollister, Texas after a civilian woman was kidnapped by a humanoid assailant, later identified to be an anomalous scarecrow, and forced into a vehicle.

I think just a little too much happens here. The article would probably flow better if the anomalous scarecrow was introduced a little more subtly, but I'm unsure how I can help with that. It's just a lot to take in, you know? It's a straight up exposition and we have to take the plot at face-value, which detracts from the mystery quite a bit. Leading the readers on something similar to a wild goose chase along with the cactus only to find out the scarecrow is the perpetrator at the end might make the story much better in terms of structure.

ejects an unidentified fluid from the portion of its body that's in between its arms. This fluid lands in the basket that holds plastic Starbucks branded cups for sale.

That's weird, what was that meant to do?

It then proceeds to repeatedly slam into the door

Clarifying it as glass might make it a tad bit funnier.

I had to google what succulent section meant. Please make it clearer by saying 'Succulent Plants section' instead, that might make it less confusing for readers with no prior knowledge of stuff like this.

Scrankle Sale Barn in Hollister, Texas where it illegally obtained a horse

Add a comma after the Texas.

And… I'm done reading it.

Hmm, I feel like the interaction between Lana, Scarecrow and Cactus could have been better. It's like, you built the suspense well and I was quite interested to see where it led, but everything was stated so plainly that I didn't really feel satisfied with it. If there was a more subtle introduction of mystery and the big 'Bam! They're just toys that are jealous!' reveal, it would be much more elegant. However, although I did feel the tension, I wasn't really worried for Lana? Most of the concern is coming from Prixor here and we have to just take it because that's all that's stated outright.

The only thing this piece suffers from is admittedly, the short word count for what could be a great narrative. You decided to go with a give-away-all-the-plot-through-ramblings-of-the-characters approach and it bogs down the rest of the story. What you need is more danger, more wacky stuff (we're talking about a pinata and doll that turned into enemies here!), and more subtle writing.

Moving on, the last log didn't really do much for me? It didn't add anything so I think you can just outright remove it, or just revamp it so that it flows into the next part of the story, maybe.

Overall, kinda funny, but still not ready for the mainsite.

item.title: Re: prix0rs the Cactus
item.content:encoded:
Text
– hide block

In fairness, most of this is fairly nitpicky - take that for what you will.

SCP-XXXX's other anomalous properties include mild telekinesis that mimics the usage, length and approximate strength of two human arms, the ability to levitate 2 meters in the air and 'swing' itself at its opponents.

I'm an Oxford comma fan - I read this as "(mild…arms), (the ability…opponents)," meaning it's missing a conjunction. Or, if levitation and swinging are two separate traits, a comma after "air."

SCP-XXXX was initially seen in the neighborhood of Sprucelude Acres in Hollister, Texas
It then traveled 6 kilometers across the city of Holston, Texas

I'm guessing the second is also supposed to be Hollister?

<Leaps onto counter, scattering specks of soil onto counter.>

Counter twice here just reads kinda clunky to me.

It later fell asleep. The following morning, a customer attempted to purchase SCP-XXXX. It noticed SCP-XXXX-1 embedded in the soil in its pot and, believing it was a toy, pulled the trigger

I had to read this twice before I understood (I think) that the customer is the one pulling the trigger? Or did the cactus somehow acquire the anomalous gun while sleeping? OR, popping back up here after I made it to the bottom again, did the cactus just not notice the gun until that point, akin to not noticing the picture was sticking out of its pot? I just don't know.

It rode the horse 194,121 meters

Super specific. You use kilometers elsewhere in the article, is there any particular importance of these numbers? It doesn't seem to fit to switch to meters here, especially since it's quite the distance.

It spots Lana Ringle and the scarecrow

We've yet to be introduced to this scarecrow. Following the log, this makes sense, but it reads weird to me to just call it "the scarecrow" at this point. It's like it's assumptive that we should already know what this is.

Opinions
– hide block

This is one of those that just doesn't vibe with me. I've seen plenty of similar articles (by way of tone and humor, that is), and they clearly work. I'm just very humorless as a rule. I totally see what you're going for, and you hit the bullseye; I'm just not the right target.

That being said, I do see how it could hit well. I'm hesitant to say a whole lot, honestly, because humor is so subjective. I'd personally call it "cute," or "kitsch" (but without all the negative connotations I wasn't aware of until I googled how to spell that properly). But, if others have said that it's funny, I'd trust them in that regard.

I'd give it a +1 for meeting my arbitrary criteria, but it also wouldn't be one of the articles I'd be excited about, or keen on linking to other people expressly to promote it.

item.title: Re: prix0rs the Cactus
item.content:encoded:
+ Text critique
- Text critique

SCP-XXXX is an abnormally small saguaro cactus (Carnegiea gigantiea) at approximately two meters with two arms

Split this sentence and reformat a bit. Try:
SCP-XXXX is a saguaro cactus (Carnegiea gigantiea) standing at approximately two meters in height. Two arms extend from the central portion of its body…

hovering 0.3 meters above the floor.

I'm not sure what this means.

and the ability to heal injuries by heavy exposure to sunlight.

This is unclear.

Discovery: SCP-XXXX was discovered when reports of a talking cactus in the Chihuahuan Desert in the state of Texas had brought the possibility of anomalous activity to the Foundation's attention.

If it's potted why would it be in the desert? This feels unnecessary.

Philips: Yeah and it's…riding a horse.

Isn't it potted?

phlegm-like fluid ejects from its 'face' and strikes Philips in the eye.

You don't explain what this 'face' is, do so in the description.

due to SCP-XXXX's telekinesis.

Implied and unneeded.

+ Overall critique
- Overall critique

I'm not feeling this for a few reasons. I'll go in-depth but it's mainly due to the narrative, structure, and dialogue.

Narrative
The issue here is that you open a few threads and never tie them up. You give us XXXX's overconfidence and obliviousness, XXXX's relationship with the scarecrow and Lana, and SCP-XXXX's cowboy tendencies and how they interact in the modern world. You set these up but never finish them.

For the overconfidence/obliviousness, we're given two addenda and neither are that funny. It's also not used to forward the narrative in any meaningful way other than XXXX not understanding something and doing it wrong. It manages to drive a car and crashes it, it thinks a fire hydrant is a cactus, it breaks a thermostat, so on. None of these comedic beats/characterization moments should both connect me to XXXX and forward the plot, they neither in the long run. The cowboy trait of XXXX is also quickly glossed over after it loses the horse. By the end, I just read about an idiotic cowboy cactus and am left saying "so what"

XXXX's relationship with the scarecrow and Lana is left at what I could barely describe as a cliffhanger. Lana says pretty much the same thing about her shop four times in a row and doesn't give us any new information to make me understand the connection. There's also the fact that I have nothing but a vague idea of what this rivalry is about. Develop this further, this is where you will bridge the characters to the reader. Focus on this.

SCP-XXXX's cowboy tendencies basically boil down to it shoots things. There's so much you can do with a fish-out-of-water character that isn't tapped into here.

Overall, there is a lack of connection between all the addendums, they make it so I am unable to connect with the characters along with the fact that there aren't many comedic moments. My advice, focus on SCP-XXXX's connection with Lana and the Scarecrow, explain to us why there's this rivalry, perhaps make the Scarecrow the straightman against the Cactus idiot, and/or explain their origins. It feels like you're trying many different forms of humor, there's absurdist with the explosions, set-up-punchline in the dialogue, slapstick with the fight, etc. You're speaking yourself thin.

A specific thing I'd like to note is that explosions for the sake of explosions feel both unwarranted and not too funny.

Structure
This one is short and will probably end up being unneeded if you take my above advice. The third addendum is out of place and should be combined with either the discovery section or the beginning of the first addendum.

Dialogue
This is going to be the make or break factor of this article. Natural dialogue is a bit tricky so I will point out some examples where my suspension of disbelief was broken:

If I can get a carriage that doesn't need no horse, then I can go fast whenever and wherever I need! Ain't even gotta water it or pick up its doo-doo!

Both unfunny and unnatural

You should be worrying more about your own safety first! In fact, why are you in a shack in the middle of the Chihuahuan Desert? <Looks past elderly woman to see trinkets and souvenirs on display.> Wait, did you say 'shop'?

Feels like you were going for the stating-the-obvious form of humor, this would be better if left as a quirk of the anomaly, or change the location altogether.

No, dearie. You're not my grandson. You're fired.

Confusing because of the lack of backstory.

Oh, I'd love to purchase this guy!

I don't think people talk like this.

That's the nicest thing anybody's ever said about me! Shoot, my old lady Lana can't even call me that anymore! 'cause she went blind!

Not funny and a bit odd.

A rewrite of problematic dialogue will probably come with the addition of my proposed changes. Remember to speak the lines out loud, if you can't imagine yourself saying it, even if you are a cowboy cactus, it should be rewritten or cut.

item.title: Re: prix0rs the Cactus
item.content:encoded:
Requested trade.

「Line by Line」
「Close」

SCP-XXXX is an abnormally short saguaro cactus1 (approximately 2 meters) with two arms.

The footnote isn't entirely needed and can be combined. Additionally, there's a bit of inconsistency. You use [2 meters] then switch to [two arms], two is written differently in the same sentence. > [SCP-XXXX is an abnormally large saguaro cactus (Carnegiea gigantiea) at approximately two meters with two arms.]

It is planted in an orange ceramic pot and it is always seen hovering .3 meters above the floor.

Could probably cut down a bit: [It is planted in an orange ceramic pot, hovering 0.3 meters above the floor.]

It has an accent that varies between individuals who hear it.

Describe the accents. What accents do people hear? European? Canadian? Californian?

While its method of communication is predominantly telepathic, voice recording technology is capable of recording a corrupted version of its speech. (See addenda.)

Combine the brackets. [of its speech (See Addendum XXXX-1 or -2, specify).]

SCP-XXXX's anomalous properties include

A cactus being sentient and can talk via telepathy is already anomalous. Maybe reword this to fit [Other anomalous qualities.]

bullets with a trajectory that is not affected by wind

I suggest: [bullets with a trajectory unaffected by wind.]

Reports of a talking cactus in the Chihuahuan Desert in the state of Texas had brought the possibility of anomalous activity to the Foundation's attention.

It feels like you're missing something here. I suggest adding [SCP-XXXX was discovered when-].

See addendum.

Brackets.

Field agents Egrene and Philips arrive at Chihuahuan Desert. Thick plumes of sand dirt are thrown into the air as SCP-XXXX hurtles through the blizzard.>

Missed formatting at the beginning. Also, add a [the] before Chihuahuan.

field agents.">

You have a quote here.

in the soil>

Missed a period.

SCP-XXXX: Where are you, you no good, job-stealing crow toilet?!
<Explosions sporadically occur within a 15 meter radius of SCP-XXXX's gunfire.>

You missed a paragraph break here. I also suggest adding a dash between [15] and [meter.]

Stop There's no need for that!

Maybe add a comma after [Stop], or a exclamation mark. Anything that signals a short break, since the next word is capitalized, and makes it flow better.

Egrene: Th-thank you…

This feels a bit stilted. Maybe something like [Thanks…?] would work better.

As a sidenote, even if it sort of makes sense in-universe to keep records of an untranslated version, I don't see what it adds to this? It feels like it's there to take up space, and if it's not essential to the narrative, I suggest you just cut it.

「Overall」
「Close」

Overall, it's not bad. It knows what it does, and gets that job done well. I think the initial encounter could be improved a bit. I can tell you were trying to go for a more satirical vibe, but that just didn't click with me. Or I could just be unfunny. That aside, I think alright in its current state. I don't feel like you need to add anything or such. It's a short, self-contained narrative. Just spice up the humour, and I think you'll be on your way.

Because in its current state, I'd probably just leave it to a no-vote because the humor didn't land, and sort of killed it for me.
